records.public_safe_text: on [date], a call for service was dispatched to [roadway] 1604n (valero gas station) for an accident involving a car versus a pedestrian. upon arriving to the scene, i immediately noticed an elderly lady laying in the parking lot between the gas pumps and the actual store surrounded by individuals trying to provide care. i walked up and noticed that she was bleeding from the crown of her head as well as her arm. converse ems arrived immediately on scene and began [roadway] over and made contact with the driver of unit 1 (chevrolet) who was obviously shaken up who stated that as he was backing out of his parking space that was facing the store he did not notice the lady behind him in his back-up camera, nor did his vehicle alert him to anyone behind him. he also stated that he heard something when he backed up but didn't think he had hit anything because he didn't see anything in his back-up camera. i went inside the store and observed video footage of the actual accident as it occurred. i observed the female walking straight from the gas pumps which was to the right of the vehicle and towards the store. she then turned about 45 degrees and continuing to walk towards the store. at the same time the driver of unit 1 (chevrolet) was backing out of his parking spot towards the right and struck the pedestrian. once his vehicle struck her he continued to back up until the pedestrian was completely underneath his vehicle. the driver then pulled off and drove off to the left and went around the gas pumps. it appeared that her husband had flagged the driver down to notify him of what had just happened. i then conducted an information exchange between the driver of unit 1 and the pedestrians husband who was on scene [medical facility] (bamc) by city of converse ems for injuries sustained during the accident. i then cleared the call and returned back to service.

records.deidentified_narrative: while on patrol in my marked patrol police responded to a call about a pedestrian who was struck in the (h-e-b) parking lot. upon my arrival i observed unit 2 laying down on the ground in the (h-e-b) parking lot on her back in front of a marked parking stall, her right shoe was approximately 3 feet away from where she was laying. unit 1 was operating a motor vehicle in a private parking lot of (h-e-b). unit 1 drive stated he was beginning to park in a parking spot but mistakenly gave the vehicle a little too much gas. officer brusich #1040 asked unit 1 driver if he confused the break peddle for the gas, unit 1 driver said no. it appeared to myself and officer brusich #1040 that unit 1 driver misjudged the concrete parking block distance and gave the vehicle gas which got unit 1 to accelerate over the concrete parking block and hit unit 2. unit 1 then struck unit 2 on the right side of her hip and unit 1 was stopped by the (h-e-b) handicap sign which resulted in $2000 dollars' worth of damage to the (h-e-b) handicap sign. ems arrived on scene and processed it. unit 2 verbally expressed pain in her right shoulder when ems personnel helped unit 2 off the [medical facility] for non-life-threating injuries by ems in an ambulance. unit 1 driver stated he did not have a medical episode and had no observed signs of intoxication. unit 1 driver did not have any observed injuries. unit 1 had no passengers at the time of this motor vehicle accident. i spoke to tid and made det. stautzenberger #2506 aware of the incident. tid did not make the scene. i advised sgt. quinn #3014 of the incident. i gave unit 1 driver and (h-e-b) staff a case card. the (h-e-b) staff had this motor vehicle accident recorded on their active security system, and i advised (h-e-b) staff to email the video footage to tid. there were no other motor vehicles involved in this motor vehicle accident. unit 1 was safe to operate on public roads.

records.public_safe_text: while on patrol in my marked patrol police responded to a call about a pedestrian who was struck in the (h-e-b) parking lot. upon my arrival i observed unit 2 laying down on the ground in the (h-e-b) parking lot on her back in front of a marked parking stall, her right shoe was approximately 3 feet away from where she was laying. unit 1 was operating a motor vehicle in a private parking lot of (h-e-b). unit 1 drive stated he was beginning to park in a parking spot but mistakenly gave the vehicle a little too much gas. officer brusich #1040 asked unit 1 driver if he confused the break peddle for the gas, unit 1 driver said no. it appeared to myself and officer brusich #1040 that unit 1 driver misjudged the concrete parking block distance and gave the vehicle gas which got unit 1 to accelerate over the concrete parking block and hit unit 2. unit 1 then struck unit 2 on the right side of her hip and unit 1 was stopped by the (h-e-b) handicap sign which resulted in $2000 dollars' worth of damage to the (h-e-b) handicap sign. ems arrived on scene and processed it. unit 2 verbally expressed pain in her right shoulder when ems personnel helped unit 2 off the [medical facility] for non-life-threating injuries by ems in an ambulance. unit 1 driver stated he did not have a medical episode and had no observed signs of intoxication. unit 1 driver did not have any observed injuries. unit 1 had no passengers at the time of this motor vehicle accident. i spoke to tid and made det. stautzenberger #2506 aware of the incident. tid did not make the scene. i advised sgt. quinn #3014 of the incident. i gave unit 1 driver and (h-e-b) staff a case card. the (h-e-b) staff had this motor vehicle accident recorded on their active security system, and i advised (h-e-b) staff to email the video footage to tid. there were no other motor vehicles involved in this motor vehicle accident. unit 1 was safe to operate on public roads.

records.deidentified_narrative: while on patrol police responded to the above location for a possible accident major involving a pedestrian. upon making the location i made contact with the pedestrian who was being seen by safd. per safd they stated that he only had minor injuries. i spoke with the pedestrian. he stated that he had parked his vehicle and while attempting to get to a spot where he could cross the cross walk, he was struck by unit 1 who had been making a right turn. per the pedestrian unit 1 stopped and the driver exited the vehicle to check on him. after checking on him unit 1 driver would then leave the location without calling police or giving any info. i was able to get unit 1's info from a witness and police were able to track down unit 1 driver. unit 1 driver would give his info and advised that he had not known that he needed to stay for the accident. tid detectives were on-scene during this time and conducted their investigation.
